title: Lamb chops on creamy spinach and butter beans

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Lamb, onions, garlic, apples, tinned butter beans, crème fraîche and spinach are all ordinary cupboard, fridge or garden foods.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is a normal Tesco line, and spring lamb chops in April are within an everyday family shop.

basic_kitchen.reason: Only a large roasting tray is needed and the technique is simple roasting and stirring.

works.reason: The chops roast for 23 minutes in total at 220°C, which would leave ordinary lamb chops dry and grey, and the Bramley wedges would collapse into sour mush through the creamy beans; stirring 600g of raw spinach on a tray outside the oven 'until it wilts' would also be slow and messy.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes covers the onion, garlic and apple prep and the stirring, and 10 + 15 + 8 matches the 33 minutes of cook time.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A large 600g bed of creamy spinach with spring lamb suits mid-April, and the spinach is a main part of the dish rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps read as plain, friendly British instructions a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Lamb, beans and a lot of spinach make a proper, filling family dinner.
